chunks: Hammad ibn Isa from Ubayd ibn Zurarah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): He asked him about two men, one of whom stood praying until morning and the other was sitting supplicating; which of them is superior?
ai.seo_question: Which is more virtuous: continuous prayer or supplication?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) ruled that the supplicant is superior to the one engaged in continuous prayer (Qiyam) until morning, emphasizing that the active, conscious engagement of du'a holds greater merit than mere physical endurance. This hadith, found in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, underscores the Shia scholarly view that du'a is not merely a request but a profound act of worship and connection with the Divine, often prioritized over ritualistic repetition when it involves heartfelt presence. It highlights the balance between ritual prayer (Salat) and personal supplication (Du'a), with the latter being a direct line of communication that reflects the believer's constant awareness of God.
